section: Solid waste, plastic waste, e-waste, biomedical and construction waste - rules and management
subsections: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types
AP waste bodies - APEMC, Clean Andhra Pradesh

accepted.s: With reference to waste-management hierarchy, which one of the following is placed at the top?
accepted.x: Source reduction means generating less waste and occupies the top position in the waste-management hierarchy.
accepted.tq: Apply the hierarchy to identify the preventive measure.
accepted.sec: 3Rs and circular economy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fly ash can be used in bricks, cement and roads.
2. The use of fly ash in these applications is noted within 300 km of thermal power plants.
3. Steel slag is used as a road aggregate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Fly ash is used in bricks, cement and roads within 300 km of thermal plants, while steel slag is used as a road aggregate.
accepted.tq: Combine closely related material-use statements and check all three facts.
accepted.sec: 3Rs and circular economy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Surat is associated with which of the following applications of industrial waste?
o: A railway line constructed using plastic certificates
A dam constructed entirely using fly ash
A landfill constructed using PET resin
A road constructed using steel slag
accepted.x: Surat has a road made using steel slag, which is used as a road aggregate.
accepted.tq: Location-based recall with a material-use trap.
accepted.sec: 3Rs and circular economy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best illustrates the contribution of biomining of legacy waste to a circular economy?
o: It permanently stores all waste without recovery.
It increases the generation of mixed municipal waste.
It recovers useful materials from old waste dumps for productive reuse.
It replaces source reduction with open dumping.
accepted.x: Biomining of legacy waste supports the circular economy by recovering materials from old waste accumulations for reuse or further processing.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that reflects resource recovery and circularity.
accepted.sec: 3Rs and circular economy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are associated with the Waste to Wealth Mission?
1. Swachhta Saarthi Fellowships
2. Su-Dhara programme
3. Plastic certificates as a replacement for all recycling
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Swachhta Saarthi Fellowships and the Su-Dhara programme are associated with the Waste to Wealth Mission. Plastic certificates are a feature of the later plastic-waste framework, not a replacement for all recycling.
accepted.tq: Find the false additional statement in a three-item combination.
accepted.sec: 3Rs and circular economy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Resin code)
 a. 1
 b. 2
 c. 3
 d. 5
List-II (Plastic)
 i. PVC
 ii. PP
 iii. PET
 iv. HDPE
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Resin code 1 denotes PET, 2 denotes HDPE, 3 denotes PVC and 5 denotes PP.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure resin-code pair and eliminate inconsistent combinations.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the resin code with the plastic type?
accepted.x: Resin code 4 denotes LDPE. Code 5 denotes PP, 6 denotes PS and 7 denotes other plastics, including polycarbonate.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent resin-code classifications.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bisphenol A (BPA) is particularly associated with which resin-code category?
accepted.x: Resin code 7 covers other plastics, including polycarbonate, in whose manufacture BPA is a concern.
accepted.tq: Link a chemical concern with the correct resin category.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016
B. Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2021
C. EPR Guidelines, 2022
D. Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026
accepted.x: The sequence is 2016 Rules, 2021 Amendment Rules, 2022 EPR Guidelines and 2026 Amendment Rules.
accepted.tq: Use the years as the first and last anchors, then place the middle instruments.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the carry-bag thickness progression under the specified plastic-waste measures?
o: 40 microns in 2011, 75 microns in 2016, 50 microns from 30 September 2021 and 120 microns from 31 December 2022
40 microns in 2011, 50 microns in 2016, 120 microns from 30 September 2021 and 75 microns from 31 December 2022
50 microns in 2011, 40 microns in 2016, 75 microns from 31 December 2021 and 120 microns from 30 September 2022
40 microns in 2011, 50 microns in 2016, 75 microns from 30 September 2021 and 120 microns from 31 December 2022
accepted.x: The stated progression is 40 microns in 2011, 50 microns in 2016, 75 microns from 30 September 2021 and 120 microns from 31 December 2022.
accepted.tq: Track a sequence of dated numerical thresholds without reversing the dates.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2021 were notified on 12 August 2021 as:
accepted.x: The 2021 amendment was notified on 12 August 2021 as GSR 571(E).
accepted.tq: Direct recall of an official notification identifier.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The ban on identified single-use plastic items came into effect from:
accepted.x: The ban on identified single-use plastic items came into effect on 1 July 2022.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ban date from the separate thickness-transition dates.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the identified single-use plastic items listed for prohibition?
o: Plastic sticks used in ear buds
accepted.x: Plastic ear-bud sticks, plastic flags and thermocol for decoration are included in the listed SUP items. HDPE milk bottles are not included in that list.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the specified SUP list rather than choosing a prohibited item.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following items:
1. Balloon sticks
2. Candy and ice-cream sticks
3. Wrapping film on sweet boxes and cigarette packets
4. PVC banners below 100 microns
Which of the above are included in the identified single-use plastic list?
accepted.x: All four listed items are included: balloon sticks, candy and ice-cream sticks, specified wrapping film, and PVC banners below 100 microns.
accepted.tq: Test completeness of a statutory list through an all-inclusive option.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Extended Producer Responsibility under the plastic-packaging framework?
o: Producers, Importers and Brand Owners handle covered plastic packaging not included in the SUP ban.
It transfers all plastic-waste responsibility to municipal bodies.
It applies only to consumers who purchase plastic goods.
It applies only to manufacturers of rigid plastics.
accepted.x: EPR applies to Producers, Importers and Brand Owners, or PIBOs, for plastic packaging not covered by the SUP ban.
accepted.tq: Ask who bears the responsibility and identify the correct institutional actors.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: EPR was first introduced into Indian waste law through the:
accepted.x: EPR first entered Indian waste law through the E-waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the exact first-introduction instrument rather than a later plastic-specific rule.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The EPR Guidelines for plastic packaging became effective in:
accepted.x: The EPR Guidelines, 2022 for plastic packaging became effective in July 2022.
accepted.tq: Separate the guideline year from its effective month.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026:
1. Plastics are classed as rigid, flexible and multi-layered.
2. Unmet targets may be carried forward for up to three years.
3. Plastic certificates become tradable.
4. Waste-to-energy, co-processing and waste-to-oil are permitted as end-of-life options.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2026 amendment includes all four measures: classification into three categories, three-year carry-forward, tradable certificates and specified end-of-life options.
accepted.tq: Check whether every provision in a regulatory amendment is correctly included.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026 were announced on:
accepted.x: The 2026 amendment was announced on 31 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the announcement date from dates associated with related reporting.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the 2026 framework, recycled content in rigid plastics is scheduled to rise from 30% to:
accepted.x: The recycled-content requirement for rigid plastics rises from 30% to 60% by 2028-29.
accepted.tq: Match the percentage target with its specified future year.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match the plastic category with its recycled-content target progression:
List-I (Category)
 a. Rigid
 b. Flexible, single-layer
 c. Multi-layered
List-II (2025-26 to later)
 i. 5% to 10%
 ii. 10% to 20%
 iii. 30% to 60%
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Rigid plastics have a 30% to 60% progression, flexible single-layer plastics 10% to 20%, and multi-layered plastics 5% to 10%.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive rigid-plastic percentage and complete the remaining pairs.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the reuse targets for rigid packaging in 2025-26?
o: 10% for small containers and 70% for large water packaging
30% for small containers and 50% for large water packaging
20% for small containers and 60% for large water packaging
70% for small containers and 10% for large water packaging
accepted.x: The reuse targets are 10% for small containers and 70% for large water packaging in 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing paired percentage targets.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the centralised CPCB EPR portal is correct?
o: It is maintained exclusively by the State Pollution Control Boards.
Recyclers generate EPR certificates and sell them to producers.
Only municipal bodies can generate EPR certificates on it.
Producers sell certificates directly to consumers without recycler participation.
accepted.x: On the centralised CPCB EPR portal, recyclers generate EPR certificates and sell them to producers.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct role of each participant in the EPR mechanism.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As of 29 October 2025, which one of the following combinations is associated with the EPR system?
o: 69,470 producers, 354 recyclers and approximately 4,402 LMT of waste recycled
35,470 producers, 4,402 recyclers and approximately 69 LMT of waste recycled
69,470 producers, 4,402 recyclers and approximately 354 LMT of waste recycled
4,402 producers, 69,470 recyclers and approximately 354 LMT of waste recycled
accepted.x: The reported figures were 69,470 registered producers, 4,402 registered recyclers and approximately 354 LMT of waste recycled across EPR streams.
accepted.tq: Match multiple quantitative indicators without interchanging their categories.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched as a hidden source of plastic?
accepted.x: Tea bags and chewing gum are among the hidden sources of plastic. Other examples include wet wipes, glitter, cigarette filters, polyester clothing and cosmetic microbeads.
accepted.tq: Recognise less-obvious plastic sources instead of conventional plastic articles.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: QR-code traceability for plastic packaging under the stated 2026 framework became mandatory from:
accepted.x: QR-code traceability became mandatory from July 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a compliance-start date from the year of the amendment.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an end-of-life option specifically mentioned under the 2026 plastic-waste framework?
accepted.x: Waste-to-energy, co-processing and waste-to-oil are mentioned end-of-life options. Open burning is not one of them.
accepted.tq: Identify the prohibited or unlisted option among specified waste-treatment routes.
accepted.sec: Plastic waste - PWM Rules and amendments, SUP ban, EPR, thickness, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the urban local-government set-up in Andhra Pradesh mentioned for waste management?
o: 17 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards
113 Municipal Corporations, 17 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards
7 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 17 cantonment boards
17 Municipal Corporations, 7 municipalities and 113 cantonment boards
accepted.x: The stated urban set-up consists of 17 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards.
accepted.tq: Keep the three administrative counts matched with their correct categories.
accepted.sec: AP waste bodies - APEMC, Clean Andhra Pradesh  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Operation Clean Sweep, launched in May 2026, is a campaign of the Municipal Administration Department for:
o: Scientific solid-waste management in Tier-1 and Tier-2 corporations
Only coastal plastic clean-up in villages
accepted.x: Operation Clean Sweep is the Municipal Administration Department’s campaign for scientific solid-waste management in Tier-1 and Tier-2 corporations.
accepted.tq: Link the campaign with its department, timing and operational scope.
accepted.sec: AP waste bodies - APEMC, Clean Andhra Pradesh  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Anantapur is setting up a 170 tonnes-per-day waste-processing plant. Guthikondavaripalem yard in Ongole is associated with biomining.
accepted.tq: Use the location-action pair to distinguish two Andhra Pradesh waste projects.
accepted.sec: AP waste bodies - APEMC, Clean Andhra Pradesh  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ongole is associated with which of the following solid-waste management activities?
o: Operating the centralised CPCB EPR portal
Setting up a 170 TPD waste-processing plant
accepted.x: Ongole is biomining its Guthikondavaripalem waste yard. The 170 TPD waste-processing plant is associated with Anantapur.
accepted.tq: Apply the location-based elimination method to nearby waste projects.
